glosses: to bother, to disturb

examples.text: Я не хочу́ тебя́ беспоко́ить.
examples.translation: I don't want to bother you.
examples.english: I don't want to bother you.

glosses: нарушать покой; доставлять хлопоты

examples.text: Никогда не беспокой другого тем, что ты можешь сам сделать.
— Иван Антонович, у меня к вам большая, большая просьба… — Денег? — Право, совестно вас беспокоить. Да мне немного, рублей с десяток.
И Якова Петровича что-то беспокоит во сне.
— Пусть и сидят в девках. — И что за беда? — Старые девки все злы делаются. — Это только те, которым очень хотелось замуж и их темперамент беспокоит.

glosses: причинять физическую боль, вызывать неприятные ощущения

examples.text: — Раны меня беспокоили в ненастье, да и надоела мне фронтовая служба…
Головная боль беспокоила больных в среднем 10,1 дня (от 1 до 30 дней), максимальная интенсивность головной боли отмечалась на 7-8-е сутки заболевания.

glosses: внушать тревогу, волновать

examples.text: Илья заметил, что болезнь деда очень беспокоит буфетчика Петруху и дядю Терентия.
Присутствие же старухи, несмотря на её глухоту, беспокоило меня.

glosses: to confuse a quiet, constant state or a calm, continuous flow, in particular: thoughts, actions or liquids.

examples.text: The noisy ventilation disturbed me during the exam.
The performance was disturbed twice by a ringing mobile phone.
A school of fish disturbed the water.

glosses: to divert, redirect, or alter by disturbing.

examples.text: A mudslide disturbed the course of the river.
The trauma disturbed his mind.
disturb his inmost counsels from their destined aim

glosses: to have a negative emotional impact; to cause emotional distress or confusion.
disturbance

examples.text: Instant without disturb they took alarm

glosses: To annoy, to disturb, to irritate; to be troublesome to, to make trouble for.

examples.text: Would it bother you if I smoked?

glosses: To annoy, to disturb, to irritate; to be troublesome to, to make trouble for.
Damn; curse.
To feel care or concern; to burden or inconvenience oneself out of concern.

examples.text: I never bother about such trivialities.
I wouldn't bother with an umbrella if I were you.

To expand, without bothering about it—without shiftless timidity on one side, or loquacious eagerness on the other—to the full compass of what he would have called a "pleasant" experience, was Newman's most definite programme of life.

glosses: To take the trouble, to trouble oneself (to do something).

examples.text: Why do I even bother to try?

glosses: To take the trouble, to trouble oneself (to do something).
To do something which is of negligible inconvenience.

examples.text: You didn’t even bother to close the door.

glosses: Fuss, ado.

examples.text: There was a bit of bother at the hairdresser's when they couldn't find my appointment in the book.
It was a 15-minute return trip to walk back home to pick up my device, but I weighed it up and decided that it wasn’t worth the bother.

glosses: Trouble, inconvenience.

examples.text: Yes, I can do that for you—it’s no bother.

glosses: A mild expression of annoyance.

examples.text: [H]e suddenly flung down his brush on the floor, said "Bother!" and "Oh blow!" and also "Hang spring-cleaning!" and bolted out of the house without even waiting to put on his coat.

"Oh, help!" said Pooh. "I'd better go back."
"Oh, bother!" said Pooh. "I shall have to go on."
"I can't do either!" said Pooh. "Oh, help and bother!"

glosses: Causar molestias o incomodidades de alguna clase.
Impedir o perturbar la correcta ejecución de una tarea.
Causar dolor ligero.
Fatigar.
Causar ira o enojo.
Causar incomodidad.
Molestar, fastidiar.
That which affects one’s welfare or happiness. A matter of interest to someone.

examples.text: Mark’s health was of great concern to Connie.

We drove back to the office with some concern on my part at the prospect of so large a case. Sunning himself on the board steps, I saw for the first time Mr. Farquhar Fenelon Cooke. He was dressed out in broad gaiters and bright tweeds, like an English tourist, and his face might have belonged to Dagon, idol of the Philistines.

Although the encounter was bathed in sunshine, the match failed to reach boiling point but that will be of little concern to Gerard Houllier’s team, who took a huge step forward before they face crucial matches against their relegation rivals.

glosses: The placement of interest or worry on a subject.

examples.text: Most people in Australia have no concern for the recent events in London.

glosses: A worry; a sense that something may be wrong; an identification of a possible problem.

examples.text: Let me know if you have any questions or concerns about the document.

glosses: The expression of solicitude, anxiety, or compassion toward a thing or person.

examples.text: Judy's eyes filled with concern as she listened to the news report.

Appleby […] rose from his seat when Morales came in. He shook hands urbanely, unbuckled his sword, and laid his kepi on the table, and then sat down with an expression of concern in his olive face which Appleby fancied was assumed.

glosses: A business, firm or enterprise; a company.

examples.text: The employees’ attitude is really hurting the concern.
a going concern
Then I remembered there was a big concern, a Company for trade on that river.
Soon after he ascended the throne, an Arabic television joint venture between the BBC and a Saudi concern, Orbit Communications, foundered over the BBC’s insistence on editorial independence.

glosses: Any set of information that affects the code of a computer program.

examples.text: At the programming level, an aspect is a modular unit that implements a concern.

glosses: To relate or belong to; to have reference to or connection with; to affect the interest of; to be of importance to.

examples.text: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ.
our wars with France have always affected us in our most tender interests, and concerned us more than those we have had with any other nation
ignorant, so far as the usual instruction was concerned

As a political system democracy seems to me extraordinarily foolish, but I would not go out of my way to protest against it. My servant is, so far as I am concerned, welcome to as many votes as he can get. I would very gladly make mine over to him if I could.

glosses: To engage by feeling or sentiment; to interest.

examples.text: A good prince concerns himself in the happiness of his subjects.
They think themselves out the reach of Providence, and no longer concerned to solicit his favour.
It had been his intention to go to Wimbledon, but as he himself said: “Why be blooming well frizzled when you can hear all the results over the wireless. And results are all that concern me.[…]”

glosses: To make somebody worried.

examples.text: I’m concerned that she’s becoming an alcoholic.

glosses: To be troubled; to give way to mental anxiety or doubt.

examples.text: So you go along for a long time / And nothing seems to worry your mind / But what it adds up to / It's the side effect / That finally gets to you

glosses: Disturb the peace of mind of; afflict with mental agitation or distress; to exercise.

examples.text: Your tone of voice worries me.
That worries the government, which fears that environmental activism could become the foundation for more general political opposition.

glosses: To harass; to irritate or distress.

examples.text: The President was worried into military action by persistent advisors.

glosses: To seize or shake by the throat, especially of a dog or wolf.

examples.text: Your dog’s been worrying sheep again.
This is the Dog, that worried the Cat, that killed the Rat, that ate the Malt, that lay in the Houſe that Jack built.

glosses: To touch repeatedly; to fiddle with.

examples.text: Christian paced the caravan, worrying his beard.
So what if I wanted to touch my nose to the windshield? Who was it hurting? Why was it that he could repeatedly worry his change and bite his lower lip without the threat of punishment?
No stories, no arguments. He just worries his prayer beads.

glosses: To strangle.

examples.text: We read (Law's Memor. Pref. lix.) that "one John Brugh, a notorious warlock (wizard) in the parochin of Fossoquhy, by the space of thirty-six years, was worried at a stake and burned, 1643."

glosses: A strong feeling of anxiety.

examples.text: I'm afflicted by worry throughout the night.
"Worry never solved any problems. Only gives you ulcers."

glosses: An instance or cause of such a feeling.

examples.text: My main worry is that I'll miss the train.

glosses: A person who causes worry.

examples.text: They could never make him speak a word, although he was old enough, in short, he was a perfect worry night and day.

glosses: Mantener fijo el pensamiento en un asunto o suceso negativo o perjudicial, que causa temor o inquietud.
Ocupar antes o anticipadamente una cosa, o prevenir a uno en la adquisición de ella.
Prevenir con anticipación el ánimo de uno, de modo que dificulte el asentir a otra opinión.
Quitar la tranquilidad.
Perturbar el derecho de alguien a poseer algo de modo tranquilo y pacífico.
niepokoić
przeszkadzać
Importuner, déranger, inquiéter.

examples.text: Я не хочу́ тебя́ беспоко́ить.
examples.translation: Je ne veux pas te déranger.
